title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 748–750). M is a profinite group. On the next page M contains a closed subgroup π, which has a 'germe de discrétification' π_0: a discrete group, defined up to commensurability, whose profinite completion is π. The model situation is clearly Longue Marche style: π is a profinite surface or Teichmüller group, π_0 its discrete version, and M an arithmetic fundamental group or the Galois-type extension of G_Q acting on π. χ_M : M → Ẑ^* plays the role of the cyclotomic character.

The data being sought are:
- an affine algebraic group G_Q of finite type over Q;
- a character χ_G : G_Q → G_m;
- a homomorphism M → G(A_Q), where A_Q here means the finite adeles over the set P of primes considered, as on p.748 (25).

The page lists the axioms such a homomorphism should satisfy.

1°) Continuity. The NB states this is equivalent to the existence of an affine flat finite-type Z-model G of G_Q such that M → G(A_Q) factors through G(Ẑ) (29). This is correct because M is compact. Its image is a compact subgroup of G(A_f). Embed G_Q in GL_n; a compact subgroup stabilises some Ẑ-lattice, hence a lattice Λ ⊂ Q^n. The schematic closure of G_Q in GL(Λ) is then a Z-model with image ⊂ G(Ẑ). The converse is clear.

2°) Compatibility with χ (30). The composite M → G(A_Q) → G_m(A_Q) = A_Q^* equals χ_M followed by the inclusion Ẑ^* ⊂ A_Q^* ⊂ ∏_{ℓ∈P} Q_ℓ^*.

3°) Compatibility with the discretification (31). For some finite-index π_0' ⊂ π_0, the composite π_0' → π → M → G(A_Q) factors through the diagonal G(Q) → G(A_Q). The NB says one may rename and take π_0' = π_0.

4°) Minimality, or 'irredundance' (finished on p.750). No proper Q-subgroup G' ⊂ G_Q has G'(A_Q) containing the image. The next page notes there is a unique smallest such G', so one can always restrict to it.

What the problem serves: this axiomatises a 'Q-structure' or 'motivic hull' for the action of an arithmetic profinite group on a discretified profinite group. It is an algebraic group over Q receiving the discrete group rationally and the profinite group adelically, compatibly with the cyclotomic character, and Zariski-minimal. In modern terms it is close to:
- the algebraic hull or Zariski closure of a compatible family of ℓ-adic images, taken simultaneously over all ℓ with a Q-structure;
- Mumford–Tate / motivic Galois group heuristics;
- relative or weighted completion of Galois groups relative to the cyclotomic character (Hain–Matsumoto).

On p.750 Grothendieck adds the commensurator G_0 of π_0 inside M, which should perhaps also map to G(Q). That is a 'discrete Galois or Teichmüller group'.
errors: χ_M is written as landing in Ẑ (with Ẑ ↪ A_Q^*). For a cyclotomic-type character it must be Ẑ^* ⊂ A_Q^*, since Ẑ is not a subgroup of A_Q^*. This is either a slip or a missing star in the handwriting.
The equivalence in the NB to 1°) uses compactness of M (M profinite, as noted on p.748). It is not stated explicitly, but it holds.
In 3°) the renaming π_0' = π_0 is harmless only because π_0 is a commensurability germ, so the axiom is really about the germ.

ideas.what: Continuity of M → G(A_f) for profinite M is equivalent to factoring through G(Ẑ) for a suitable Z-model of G_Q.
ideas.modern_name: Compact subgroups of G(A_f) lie in G(Ẑ) for some integral model

ideas.what: An algebraic group over Q with a character to G_m, receiving M adelically, compatibly with the cyclotomic character.
ideas.modern_name: Relative / weighted completion relative to the cyclotomic character; ℓ-adic Zariski closure of Galois images
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, motivic π_1 of P^1−{0,1,∞}); Hain–Matsumoto (2003, weighted completion)

ideas.what: Requirement that the discrete germ π_0 (up to finite index) maps into the rational points G(Q).
ideas.modern_name: Q-structure / arithmeticity of the discretification; Malcev or algebraic hull of π_0 compatible with the adelic hull of π

ideas.what: Minimality / irredundance: the image is not contained in G'(A) for a proper Q-subgroup, and a unique minimal G' exists.
ideas.modern_name: Adelic Zariski closure / algebraic envelope (Mumford–Tate-like hull)

missed.claim: An axiomatic notion of a single algebraic group over Q, a 'rational-adelic hull', that simultaneously receives the profinite arithmetic group M adelically (integral at almost all ℓ), receives the discrete germ π_0 rationally, and is compatible with the cyclotomic character. Grothendieck leaves open whether the commensurator of π_0 in M must also land in G(Q). This anticipates Betti/ℓ-adic comparison for relative completions, but formulated adelically for all primes at once with an integral model, rather than one prime at a time.
missed.quote: 3°). Compatibilité avec la discrétification π_0 … pour un sous-groupe d'indice fini convenable π_0' de π_0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Hain–Matsumoto and Deligne work ℓ-by-ℓ or motivically. An adelic, integral-model version tied to the commensurator of the discrete Teichmüller group (cf. Margulis' commensurator criterion) is a framing not standard in the Grothendieck–Teichmüller literature.

deep.surprise_reason: It is a clean axiomatic set-up of an adelic algebraic hull with a Q-structure on the discretification, anticipating Deligne's and Hain–Matsumoto's completions. The content on this page itself is definitional, and its closest analogues exist in the later literature.
transcription_corrections: 'la discrète factorisation π_0' should read 'la discrétification π_0' (cf. 'germe de discrétification' on the next page).
In (30) the product is ∏_{ℓ∈P} Q_ℓ^* (P the set of primes as on p.748), not ∏_{ℓ≠p}.
The domain of χ_M should presumably be Ẑ^*; the star is not visible.
'Si j'en crois' is uncertain; the opening phrase is hard to read.
